t.2.65.1: Setting out from Rājagṛha facing east, the valiant and glorious delight of the Ikṣvākus crossed the Hrādinī and the Dūrapārā, and the river Śatadrū, rippling with waves in its westward-flowing current.
t.2.65.2: Crossing the river at Elādhāna and reaching the Aparaparpaṭas, they crossed the Śilā, which carries along rocks, and also Śalyakartana, sacred to Agni.
t.2.65.3: True to his vows, pure and glorious, he gazed upon the river Śilāvahā and passed beyond the great mountains toward the Caitraratha forest.
t.2.65.4: Reaching the swift, roaring river called Kuliṅgā, hemmed in by mountains, and then the Yamunā, he crossed over and let his army rest.
t.2.65.5: Having cooled his limbs and refreshed the weary horses, he bathed there and drank, and then, taking water with him, he went on his way.
t.2.65.6: The noble prince, in his fine carriage, passed swiftly through the great, seldom-frequented forest, as the wind sweeps across the sky.
t.2.65.7: Going by the southern side, the son of Daśaratha reached Toraṇa and Jambūprastha, and then went on to Varūtha, a delightful village.
t.2.65.8: Having made a halt there in that lovely forest, he went on facing east to the garden of Ujjihānā, where the priyaka trees grow.
t.2.65.10: Having made a halt at Sarvatīrtha, and having crossed the river Uttānikā and various other rivers with horses from the mountains,
t.2.65.9: Reaching the sāla and priyaka trees, Bharata mounted swift horses, and then, taking leave of the army, he hurried on.
t.2.65.11: Reaching Hastipṛṣṭhaka, he passed beyond the Kuṭikā; and that tiger among men crossed the Kapīvatī at Lauhitya, the Sthāṇumatī at Ekasāla, and the river Gomatī at Vinata.
t.2.65.12: Then, having reached the sāla forest at the city of Kaliṅga, Bharata, his mounts utterly exhausted, came on swiftly.
t.2.65.13: Having swiftly passed beyond the forest, at the break of dawn, as the night was ending, he beheld Ayodhyā, the city built by King Manu.
t.2.65.14: Having spent seven nights on the road, that tiger among men, seeing the city of Ayodhyā before him, spoke to the charioteer in the chariot.
t.2.65.15: O charioteer, this glorious Ayodhyā, with its holy gardens and its pale earth, seen from afar, does not look at all pleasing to me.
t.2.65.17: Formerly in Ayodhyā a great and tumultuous sound of men and women was heard on every side; today I do not hear it.
t.2.65.16: It was thronged with sacrificers and with virtuous brāhmaṇas who had mastered the Vedas, most of them prosperous, and it was protected by the foremost of royal seers.
t.2.65.18: For at other times, in the evening, the gardens appear bright to me, filled with men who, having played and then ceased, run about on every side.
t.2.65.20: For here the chief men are no longer seen, as before, going out or coming in by chariots, by elephants, or by horses.
t.2.65.19: Forsaken by their lovers, those places seem today to be weeping; O charioteer, the city appears to me as though it had become a wilderness.
t.2.65.21: I see omens of many kinds, unwelcome, evil and unpleasing; therefore my mind sinks in despondency.
t.2.65.22: With his mounts exhausted, he entered by the Vaijayanta gate. Hailed with "Victory!" by the doorkeepers, who rose to greet him, he went on accompanied by them.
t.2.65.24: O charioteer, the signs that we heard of long ago, such as appear at the death of kings, all of them I now see here.
t.2.65.23: But Rāghava, his heart troubled and unsettled, returned the greetings of the people standing at the gate, and there he spoke to Aśvapati's weary charioteer.
t.2.65.25: In the city I see the people, men and women alike, soiled and with eyes full of tears, wretched, lost in brooding, emaciated, and filled with anxious longing.
t.2.65.26: Having spoken thus to the charioteer, Bharata, dejected in mind, beheld those inauspicious sights in Ayodhyā and went on to the king's palace. Seeing that city, once radiant as Indra's city, with its crossroads, houses and streets deserted and the bolts and panels of its gates reddened with dust, he was filled all the more with grief.
t.2.65.27: Seeing many things displeasing to the mind, which had never been in his city at any other time, the great-souled one, with head bowed, dejected in spirit and joyless, entered the dwelling of his father.
